tips.author: Excel Formula Assistant
tips.title: Absolute references stop ranges from moving
tips.body: Press F4 while editing a reference to add dollar signs, for example $A$1:$A$10. When you drag the formula down, the reference stays fixed instead of shifting.

tips.author: Excel Formula Assistant
tips.title: Double-click the fill handle to fill instantly
tips.body: Select a cell with a formula and double-click the small square at its bottom-right corner. Excel fills the formula down as far as there is adjacent data.

tips.author: Excel Formula Assistant
tips.title: Use named ranges for readable formulas
tips.body: Select a range, type a name such as Sales in the Name Box, then write =SUM(Sales). The formula becomes readable and does not break when rows are inserted.

tips.author: Community example
tips.title: Exam pass rate in one formula
tips.body: If marks are in B2:B60: =ROUND(COUNTIF(B2:B60, ">=50")/COUNT(B2:B60)*100, 1)&"%" gives the pass percentage directly.

tips.author: Community example
tips.title: Month-wise sales summary
tips.body: Put month numbers 1-12 in a column and use =SUMIFS($D$2:$D$1000, $A$2:$A$1000, $E2) where column A stores =MONTH(date). Each row totals one month.

tips.author: Excel Formula Assistant
tips.title: Short keys for editing formulas
tips.body: F2 edits the active cell, Ctrl+` shows all formulas instead of results, and F9 evaluates a selected part of a formula while editing.

tips.author: Community example
tips.title: Extract domain from email
tips.body: =MID(A2, FIND("@", A2) + 1, LEN(A2)) returns everything after the @ sign.

tips.author: Excel Formula Assistant
tips.title: Keep data clean before calculating
tips.body: Wrap imported columns with =TRIM(CLEAN(A2)) to remove stray spaces and control characters that break lookups.
